paragraphs.en: 'Our fates are now intertwined'
paragraphs.zh: “我们的命运如今紧紧交织”

paragraphs.en: For many years now, the majority of the Guardian's audience has come from outside the UK.
paragraphs.zh: 多年以来，《卫报》的大部分读者都来自英国境外。

paragraphs.en: We originally found a global audience by accident.
paragraphs.zh: 我们当初收获全球读者实属偶然。

paragraphs.en: After 9/11, as the US launched the "war on terror", many American readers found their own media was speaking with one voice, and sought out the Guardian's journalism on the newish internet.
paragraphs.zh: 九一一事件之后，美国发起“反恐战争”，许多美国读者发现本国媒体论调高度统一，于是在当时尚属新兴的互联网上找到《卫报》的报道。

paragraphs.en: Then as now, they wanted something distinctive.
paragraphs.zh: 彼时和如今一样，他们想要与众不同的内容。

paragraphs.en: Our international reporting is not filtered through the lens of the state department or the Foreign Office or any government's ministry for foreign affairs.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的国际报道不会经过美国国务院、英国外交部或任何国家外事部门的立场过滤。

paragraphs.en: Our reporting on South America or Africa or the Middle East is not narrowly focused on what each story means for the US or the UK, nor does it centre the perspective of the powerful in those places.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对南美、非洲、中东的报道，不会狭隘地只聚焦每件事对美英两国的影响，也不会只站当地权势阶层的视角叙事。

paragraphs.en: We report on what matters to the ordinary people who live there and for audiences like them around the world.
paragraphs.zh: 我们报道当地普通人关切的事，写给全球和他们处境相似的读者。

paragraphs.en: We aim, too, to connect the dots between different countries, to offer a broader perspective.
paragraphs.zh: 我们也力求串联起各国之间的关联，提供更宏大的视野。

paragraphs.en: Take our recent piece about the policies of New York's new mayor.
paragraphs.zh: 举个我们近期关于纽约新任市长政策的报道为例。

paragraphs.en: Its headline was "Europeans recognise Zohran Mamdani's supposedly radical policies as 'normal'" – and it was a reminder to American readers that free buses and universal childcare are nothing unusual in some parts of the world.
paragraphs.zh: 文章标题为《欧洲人眼中，佐兰·马达尼这套看似激进的政策实则稀松平常》——这篇报道提醒美国读者，免费公交、全民育儿保障在世界部分地区早已普及，并无新奇之处。

paragraphs.en: So part of our job is to connect our global audience together, not by flattening the world out and presenting the bland view from nowhere, but by illuminating many somewheres.
paragraphs.zh: 因此我们的一部分使命是联结全球读者，不是抹平世界差异、输出空洞无地域立场的平庸观点，而是展现世界各地多样的真实面貌。

paragraphs.en: And what is striking is just how much these somewheres have in common, despite all their rich idiosyncrasies.
paragraphs.zh: 而令人触动的是，尽管各地风土人情千差万别，这些地方却有着大量共通困境。

paragraphs.en: It's not surprising when you think about it.
paragraphs.zh: 细想之下，这并不难理解。

paragraphs.en: The crises I described earlier have little regard for national borders. They affect us all.
paragraphs.zh: 前文提到的各类危机从来不受国境束缚，所有人都会受其波及。

paragraphs.en: As Guardian columnist Nesrine Malik wrote recently: "What I have learned as the world order begins to fray is that all our fates are now intertwined.
paragraphs.zh: 《卫报》专栏作家内斯琳·马利克近期写道：“随着世界旧秩序逐步瓦解，我意识到所有人的命运如今都紧紧交织。

paragraphs.en: Energy supply disruptions, the movement of refugees and expanding military conflict are no longer foreign stories, but domestic ones."
paragraphs.zh: 能源供应中断、难民迁徙、不断蔓延的军事冲突，早已不再是他国新闻，而是和我们自身息息相关的本土议题。”

paragraphs.en: We are global but, at the same time, we have roots. You have to be rooted to rise.
paragraphs.zh: 我们立足全球视野，同时扎根本土根基。唯有扎根沃土，方能登高望远。

paragraphs.en: The Guardian was founded in Manchester, in the north of England, in 1821 and moved to London only in 1964.
paragraphs.zh: 《卫报》1821年创立于英格兰北部的曼彻斯特，1964年才迁至伦敦。

paragraphs.en: As a northerner, I know how much that matters.
paragraphs.zh: 身为北方人，我深知这份本土根基意义重大。

paragraphs.en: In recent years, we have dramatically increased the size of our Manchester office, and have many more reporters based outside London and around the UK than we had a decade ago.
paragraphs.zh: 近些年，我们大幅扩充曼彻斯特分社规模，派驻伦敦以外、遍布全英各地的记者数量，较十年前翻了数倍。

paragraphs.en: Many somewheres. We also believe in holding ourselves accountable.
paragraphs.zh: 扎根万千土地。我们同时坚持自我问责。

paragraphs.en: In 2023, we launched our Cotton Capital project, which investigates how the original funders of the Guardian made much of their wealth through transatlantic slavery.
paragraphs.zh: 2023年，我们启动《棉花资本》专题项目，调查《卫报》早期出资人如何依靠跨大西洋奴隶贸易积累大量财富。

paragraphs.en: This was not just a one-off project, but a long-term commitment.
paragraphs.zh: 这并非一次性短期项目，而是长期持续的工作。

paragraphs.en: It is reflected in our journalism – through our expanded coverage of Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, and through our newsletter The Long Wave, which covers the lives, culture and politics of the Black diaspora.
paragraphs.zh: 这份态度体现在我们的新闻报道之中：扩充非洲、拉美、加勒比地区报道版面，推出聚焦黑人散居族群生活、文化与政治的专栏《长波》。

paragraphs.en: And it is reflected in Legacies of Enslavement, our 10-year restorative justice initiative, which seeks to build partnerships with descendant communities in Jamaica, and the Sea Islands in the US, where the Guardian's early funders had links.
paragraphs.zh: 同时落地为期十年的修复正义项目《奴隶制遗留》，与牙买加、美国海岛等《卫报》早期资方曾涉足的地区的黑奴后裔社群建立合作。

paragraphs.en: As journalists, we are part of the societies we report on, not observers watching from above.
paragraphs.zh: 身为新闻从业者，我们是所报道社会的一份子，而非居高临下的旁观者。

paragraphs.en: This means our staff should reflect the world they are covering.
paragraphs.zh: 这意味着编辑部人员构成应当映照我们所记录的多元世界。

paragraphs.en: The shift in attitudes to the idea of diversity has been dramatic in the past couple of years.
paragraphs.zh: 过去两年，社会各界对多元包容理念的态度发生巨大转变。

paragraphs.en: Companies and brands that once made bold pledges have quietly dropped them.
paragraphs.zh: 许多企业品牌曾经高调许下多元发展承诺，如今却悄悄搁置。

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration has criticised diversity as a "destructive", anti-meritocratic ideology and slashed federal DEI programmes while sacking women and people of colour from senior positions.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府将多元包容政策斥为“具有破坏性”、违背精英择优原则的意识形态，大幅削减联邦多元公平发展项目，同时解雇身居高层的女性与有色族裔从业者。

paragraphs.en: Rightwing populism abhors diversity, pluralism, breadth.
paragraphs.zh: 右翼民粹主义排斥多元、包容与多元视角。

paragraphs.en: But for us it is simple: the wider the range of people bringing in stories, the better and more interesting our journalism, the truer to the world around us, and the wider and deeper our audience.
paragraphs.zh: 但对我们而言道理十分简单：采编团队人员背景越丰富，新闻内容就越优质生动，越贴合真实世界，受众覆盖面也会更广、联结更深。

paragraphs.en: Let me give you an example of what I mean.
paragraphs.zh: 我举一个实例说明。

paragraphs.en: In 2024, the Guardian hired its first dedicated Caribbean correspondent, Natricia Duncan.
paragraphs.zh: 2024年，《卫报》聘用首位专职加勒比地区记者纳特里西亚·邓肯。

paragraphs.en: The following year, one of the most devastating hurricanes of recent years struck Jamaica, where Natricia is based.
paragraphs.zh: 次年，近年破坏力最强的飓风之一袭击纳特里西亚常驻的牙买加。

paragraphs.en: Hurricane Melissa was a category 5 storm, which destroyed hospitals, infrastructure and tens of thousands of homes, and left at least 90 people dead across the region.
paragraphs.zh: 五级飓风梅丽莎摧毁多家医院、公共基建与数万栋民居，整个加勒比地区至少九十人遇难。

paragraphs.en: Where other international news organisations had to fly reporters in to cover the devastation, we already had someone on the ground, who had built up the kind of contacts needed for great reporting.
paragraphs.zh: 其他国际媒体只能临时派遣记者飞赴当地报道灾情，而我们早已有人驻守一线，积累了深度报道所需的各类本地人脉资源。

paragraphs.en: Natricia was also living through this hurricane like everyone else in Jamaica.
paragraphs.zh: 纳特里西亚和所有牙买加民众一样，亲身经历了这场飓风。

paragraphs.en: In the past, our coverage might have been limited.
paragraphs.zh: 放在过去，我们对这类灾情的报道会十分有限。

paragraphs.en: But this was a story of global importance, and now we had the resources to do it justice.
paragraphs.zh: 但这场灾害具备全球层面的重要意义，如今我们拥有充足资源完整呈现全貌。

paragraphs.en: We reported on the immediate impact on communities, the role the climate crisis played in the devastation, the effects of the storm months afterwards, and how Caribbean countries are preparing for the next hurricane season.
paragraphs.zh: 我们报道飓风对社区造成的即时冲击、气候危机在此次灾难中扮演的推手作用、飓风数月后持续遗留的影响，以及加勒比各国为下一个飓风季做出的防灾筹备。

paragraphs.en: We did not make this a story about stranded western tourists.
paragraphs.zh: 我们没有把报道重心放在受困的西方游客身上。
